title: A file's path is its ticket: retries are safe, overwrites are not
goal: Explain file-ingestion identity, then implement and compare it in Databricks Auto Loader and Snowflake Snowpipe.
concept:
Imagine a concert usher who marks each ticket number as used. The same ticket can be scanned twice without admitting two people. But if someone changes the name printed on an already-used ticket, the usher still sees the same ticket number and refuses it.

File ingestion works similarly: the service remembers a file identity, usually its path/name. Duplicate notifications do not necessarily create duplicate loads. Replacing the contents at the same path is dangerous because the ingestion memory can still say “already seen.”
example: The first event for orders/2026-10-14-18.json loads rows O-7 and O-8. A repeated event for that path is skipped. A corrected file uploaded to the same path can also be skipped. Uploading the correction as ...-18-v2.json gives it a new identity; downstream logic can then reconcile O-7 rather than blindly appending another order.

use_case.when: Use managed file ingestion when producers land immutable files in object storage and the pipeline must recover from duplicate notifications or restarts.
use_case.example: An S3 producer writes hourly order files. A notification is retried after a network timeout, and one batch later needs a correction.
use_case.decision: Treat source files as immutable, keep ingestion state durable, and publish corrections under a new path. Add business-key reconciliation because file-level exactly-once does not remove duplicates across different files.

practice: Choose each arrival scenario and predict LOAD or SKIP before revealing the remembered identity.
boundary: This local JavaScript model reduces identity to a path string. Real products have checkpoints/load metadata, permissions, retention, schema handling, concurrency and downstream table semantics. It does not contact Databricks, Snowflake or object storage.

const fileFacts={first:['orders-18.json','not seen','LOAD','remember path'],retry:['orders-18.json','seen','SKIP','no second file load'],overwrite:['orders-18.json','seen','SKIP','same identity hides correction'],version:['orders-18-v2.json','not seen','LOAD','then reconcile O-7']};let fileShown=false;function paintFile(){const f=fileFacts[fileCase.value];fileWorld.innerHTML='
Arrival
'+f[0]+'
Memory
'+(fileShown?f[1]:'predict')+'
Decision
'+(fileShown?f[2]:'?')+'
Next
'+(fileShown?f[3]:'explain why')+'
';}fileCase.onchange=()=>{fileShown=false;paintFile()};fileReveal.onclick=()=>{fileShown=true;paintFile()};paintFile();
questions: A producer sends the same object-store notification twice. What should durable file-ingestion state normally do?
Recognize the path and skip a second file load
Durable state turns notification retries into a path-level no-op.
A correction replaces bytes at an already-loaded path. Safest publishing rule?
Write a versioned path and reconcile business keys
A new identity makes the correction observable; reconciliation controls row effects.
What does file-level exactly-once fail to prove?
Two different files cannot contain the same order
Business duplicates can arrive under different paths.

steps.note: Start with empty ingestion memory and one immutable path.

steps.code:
first_action='LOAD' if path not in seen else 'SKIP'
seen.add(path)
steps.note: The first arrival loads, then the path is remembered.

steps.code: retry_action='SKIP' if path in seen else 'LOAD'
steps.note: A repeated event for the same identity is skipped.

steps.code:
corrected='orders/2026-10-14-18-v2.json'
correction_action='LOAD' if corrected not in seen else 'SKIP'
steps.note: A versioned correction has a new identity and can load.

walkthrough.limit: Executed local Python over path strings. No object store, notification service, vendor checkpoint, pipe or table was used.

visual_explanation: Read left to right: an arrival presents a path, ingestion memory answers seen/not-seen, and that answer selects LOAD or SKIP. The versioned correction changes the identity rather than decorating the same path.
written_questions: Why is an immutable source-path rule valuable even when the producer can overwrite objects?
Where would you reconcile duplicate order IDs that arrive in two different files?

product_sections.title: Databricks: Auto Loader remembers files in its checkpoint
product_sections.html:
Use case. Continuously ingest immutable JSON files from S3 into a Delta bronze table and resume after a job failure.

Prepared real lab. Use an authorized non-production workspace, external location and durable checkpoint. The SQL is unexecuted vendor practice; the visual below is a local teaching model.

CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE bronze_ordersAS SELECT *, _metadata.file_path AS source_fileFROM STREAM read_files(  's3://acme-study/orders/', format => 'json');

Failure/fix. Reusing the same source path can hide a correction. Keep files immutable, use a new path, and use a downstream MERGE on business identity if the correction must replace earlier rows. A separate source should use a separate checkpoint.
product_sections.markdown:
Use an authorized non-production workspace. SQL is unexecuted vendor practice.

```sql
CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE bronze_orders AS
SELECT *, _metadata.file_path AS source_file
FROM STREAM read_files('s3://acme-study/orders/', format => 'json');
```

Auto Loader persists discovered-file state in its checkpoint and can resume after failure. Keep inputs immutable; use a new path for a correction and reconcile downstream.

product_sections.title: Snowflake: Snowpipe remembers loaded filenames for a limited window
product_sections.html:
Use case. Auto-ingest immutable staged CSV files into a landing table while tolerating duplicate cloud events.

Prepared real lab. Use an authorized non-production database, stage, integration and warehouse context. The SQL is unexecuted vendor practice; the visual is local JavaScript.

CREATE PIPE orders_pipe AUTO_INGEST=TRUE ASCOPY INTO bronze_ordersFROM @orders_stage FILE_FORMAT=(TYPE=CSV);SELECT * FROM TABLE(INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COPY_HISTORY(  TABLE_NAME=>'BRONZE_ORDERS', START_TIME=>DATEADD('hour',-1,CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())));

Failure/fix. Snowpipe load metadata records file path/name for 14 days. The same filename can be ignored inside that window even if bytes changed; after metadata expires it can load again. Use immutable, versioned names and do not mix Snowpipe with bulk COPY for the same files unless duplication is deliberately controlled.
product_sections.markdown:
Use an authorized non-production account. SQL is unexecuted vendor practice.

```sql
CREATE PIPE orders_pipe AUTO_INGEST=TRUE AS
COPY INTO bronze_orders FROM @orders_stage FILE_FORMAT=(TYPE=CSV);
SELECT * FROM TABLE(INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COPY_HISTORY(
  TABLE_NAME=>'BRONZE_ORDERS', START_TIME=>DATEADD('hour',-1,CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())));
```

Snowpipe keeps load metadata for 14 days. Use immutable, versioned names; avoid overlapping Snowpipe and bulk COPY metadata.

Publish a versioned name, then reconcile business keys
Both products treat file identity as ingestion memory; immutability makes corrections visible.
Two different files contain order O-7. What does file-level deduplication guarantee?
Each unseen file can load once; business-key dedup is separate
The second file is automatically deleted

title: An interrupt is a stop request—do not erase it
goal: Preserve Java cancellation by understanding that InterruptedException clears the thread's interrupt flag.
concept:
An interrupt is like a hotel wake-up call: it asks the sleeper to stop waiting and check what to do next. In Java, blocking calls such as sleep throw InterruptedException and clear the interrupt status. If code catches the exception and does nothing, the outer loop may never learn that shutdown was requested.

If this layer cannot finish the cancellation itself, either rethrow InterruptedException or restore the flag with Thread.currentThread().interrupt().
example: A worker polls Kafka, batches records, then sleeps for backoff. Deployment shutdown interrupts it. The bad catch logs and retries forever. The fixed catch restores the flag, and the outer loop exits before starting another batch.

use_case.when: Use cooperative interruption for executor cancellation, service shutdown and bounded background work.
use_case.example: A rolling deployment interrupts a worker during retry backoff so it can stop before its termination grace period expires.
use_case.decision: Rethrow when the method contract allows it; otherwise restore the flag and return or let an outer owner decide. Do not use interrupt as a force-kill or assume arbitrary code will stop.

practice: Toggle the catch behavior and watch the flag after sleep, after catch, and at the loop boundary.
boundary: The browser visual is a state machine, not a Java VM or scheduler. The recorded Java example proves the documented flag changes on this runtime, not application safety under every race.
js:
function paintInterrupt(){const restore=restoreFlag.checked;interruptWorld.innerHTML='
running
flag=false
interrupt requested
flag=true
sleep throws
flag cleared
catch
flag='+(restore?'true':'false')+'
outer loop
'+(restore?'STOP':'CONTINUE')+'
';}runInterrupt.onclick=paintInterrupt;restoreFlag.onchange=paintInterrupt;paintInterrupt();
questions: What happens to interrupt status when sleep throws InterruptedException?
The blocking method clears status when it throws.
A catch cannot rethrow InterruptedException. What usually preserves cancellation?
Restoring status lets outer code observe the request.
A cooperative signal that code must handle
Interruption is cooperative, not a kill switch.

steps.note: Set the current thread's interrupt flag.

steps.code:
boolean caught=false;
try { Thread.sleep(1); } catch (InterruptedException e) { caught=true; }; boolean afterCatch=Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted();
steps.note: Sleep detects the flag, throws, and clears it.
Restore the flag so the outer owner chooses stop.

walkthrough.limit: Executed on the build Java runtime using the current thread; no executor, I/O, Kafka client or shutdown race was involved.

visual_explanation: The flag is high when interruption is requested, drops when sleep throws, and rises again only if the catch restores it. The last node shows the application consequence.
written_questions: Where in your worker should cancellation ownership live?
What cleanup must happen before the worker returns?

title: A migration ends when the old path can be removed
goal: Turn migration completion into an evidence-based decommission gate rather than a launch milestone.
concept:
Moving apartments is not finished when the new keys work. It is finished when mail is redirected, the old utilities are off, the inspection passes, and returning the old keys is safe.

A production migration needs the same exit gate: zero intended traffic on the old path, no unknown dependencies, reconciled data, a completed rollback window, named owners and stakeholder approval. Keeping the old system “just in case” indefinitely preserves cost and hidden coupling.
example: Checkout moved to a new cell. Traffic reached 100%, but a monthly finance export still reads the old database. The dependency scan blocks retirement. After the export moves, reconciliation stays green for 14 days and the fallback window closes, the gate can approve deletion.

use_case.when: Use a decommission gate after cutover for databases, services, queues, regions or vendor migrations.
use_case.example: Retire an old Kafka cluster only after producers, consumers, ACL automation, backups and disaster-recovery procedures no longer depend on it.
use_case.decision: Require measurable exit criteria and an accountable approver. Extend the window for high-impact uncertainty; do not keep the source alive merely because no owner will sign.

practice: Change old traffic, unknown dependencies and stable days. Observe which single unmet condition blocks retirement.
boundary: This model treats five gates as Boolean facts. Real migration evidence has sampling error, long-tail jobs, legal retention, asset disposal, security and rollback trade-offs.

function paintRetire(){const traffic=+oldTraffic.value,deps=+unknownDeps.value,days=+stableDays.value;oldTrafficValue.textContent=traffic;unknownDepsValue.textContent=deps;stableDaysValue.textContent=days;const gates=[['old traffic = 0',traffic===0],['unknown dependencies = 0',deps===0],['stable ≥ 14 days',days>=14],['data reconciled',true],['owner approves',true]];retireWorld.innerHTML='
'+gates.map(g=>'
'+g[0]+'
'+(g[1]?'PASS':'BLOCK')+'
').join('')+'

'+(gates.every(g=>g[1])?'RETIRE':'KEEP OLD PATH')+'

';}[oldTraffic,unknownDeps,stableDays].forEach(x=>x.oninput=paintRetire);checkRetire.onclick=paintRetire;paintRetire();
questions: New-system traffic is 100%, but one old dependency remains. Decision?
Cutover percentage alone does not prove removability.
To time-box fallback while evidence accumulates
A time-box creates a deliberate point for closing fallback.
Exit criteria pass with named approval
Multiple independent criteria reduce hidden dependency risk.

steps.note: Capture measurable retirement evidence.
Add correctness and accountability gates.

steps.code:
eligible=(old_traffic_pct==0 and unknown_dependencies==0 and stable_days>=14 and data_reconciled and owner_approved)
decision='RETIRE' if eligible else 'KEEP'
steps.note: Retire only when every required gate passes.

walkthrough.limit: Executed local Python over declared facts; it did not discover dependencies, compare data or retire infrastructure.

visual_explanation: Each box is an independent veto. The final decision changes only when every red blocker turns green, emphasizing that retirement is an AND gate.
written_questions: Which long-tail dependency in your estate is least visible to traffic dashboards?
Who is accountable for approving irreversible deletion?

title: A deprecation warning is a migration clock
goal: Respond to deprecated MCP Sampling by moving new server-side model calls to a direct provider API.
concept:
A shop can honor an old coupon while refusing to issue new ones. “Deprecated” means the path may still work, but new designs should not depend on it and existing users need a migration plan.

In the 2026-07-28 MCP specification, Sampling is deprecated. Its server-to-client backchannel does not fit the modern protocol direction. New MCP servers that need a model should call a provider API directly under explicit server-owned credentials, policy, telemetry and tests.
example: A tool server previously asked the client to sample a model. The replacement isolates a ModelGateway behind the server: production uses a provider adapter; tests inject a fake. The tool contract stays stable while auth, budgets and retries become observable.

use_case.when: Use this migration when an MCP server performs model reasoning as part of a tool operation or when upgrading to the modern MCP protocol.
use_case.example: A catalog tool summarizes schema drift after reading metadata. The server calls its configured model provider instead of asking the MCP client to sample.
use_case.decision: For new work, use a direct provider API. For existing Sampling users, inventory clients, add telemetry, introduce an adapter, migrate gradually and remove only after compatibility evidence.

practice: Switch between legacy and modern protocol modes and compare Sampling with a direct provider route.
boundary: The browser never calls an MCP client or model provider. It visualizes protocol direction and ownership, not SDK compatibility, auth, latency, model quality or cost.
js:
function paintRoute(){const modern=mcpEra.value==='modern',sampling=modelRoute.value==='sampling';const result=sampling?(modern?'NO BACKCHANNEL':'WORKS, BUT DEPRECATED'):'EXPLICIT SERVER CALL';routeWorld.innerHTML='
tool server
'+(sampling?'server → client Sampling':'server → provider adapter')+'
'+result+'
'+(sampling?'migration clock running':'credentials + policy owned here')+'
';}[mcpEra,modelRoute].forEach(x=>x.onchange=paintRoute);runRoute.onclick=paintRoute;paintRoute();
questions: Should a new MCP server adopt Sampling after the 2026-07-28 deprecation?
The specification says new implementations should not adopt deprecated features.
What should stay stable during migration?
The tool's user-facing contract where possible
An adapter can change model transport without needlessly changing the tool contract.
Client inventory, telemetry and compatibility tests
Evidence must cover real consumers and failure paths.

steps.note: Describe the protocol generation and design decision.
Record the protocol constraints.

steps.code:
route='provider_api' if new_design or not backchannel_available else 'mcp_sampling'
result='server_owned_provider_call' if route=='provider_api' else 'client_sampling'
steps.note: Choose the supported route explicitly.

visual_explanation: The center arrow is the concept: legacy Sampling points back to the client; the replacement points from the server to a provider adapter with explicit ownership.
written_questions: Which policy controls must move into the server-owned provider adapter?

title: A wider optical cone prints smaller features—but narrows focus
goal: Use the Rayleigh relationships to understand the promise and trade-off of Hyper-NA EUV research.
concept:
A camera with a wider lens opening gathers light from steeper angles and can reveal finer detail, but the region that stays sharply focused becomes thinner. EUV lithography has the same qualitative trade-off.

In the simplified Rayleigh relationships, printable size scales like k₁λ/NA, while depth of focus scales roughly like λ/NA². Raising numerical aperture improves resolution, but focus control becomes less forgiving.
example: Holding wavelength at 13.5 nm and using a teaching value k₁=0.28, NA 0.33 gives about 11.45 nm, NA 0.55 about 6.87 nm, and research-level NA 0.75 about 5.04 nm. The arithmetic is illustrative—not a scanner specification or production claim.

use_case.when: Use these relationships to reason about why lithography roadmaps raise NA and why process integration becomes harder.
use_case.example: Compare a hypothetical Hyper-NA concept with High-NA for a layer whose single-exposure resolution is limiting.
use_case.decision: Treat Hyper-NA as research until imaging, masks, resist, overlay, focus control, throughput and economics are demonstrated together.

practice: Move NA from 0.33 to 0.75. Watch resolution improve while relative focus tolerance shrinks.
boundary: This is a two-equation teaching calculator with a fixed k₁. It omits resist chemistry, aberrations, mask 3D effects, stochastic defects, overlay, throughput and cost. Hyper-NA is research, not a production scanner claim.
js:
function paintOptics(){const v=+na.value/100;naValue.textContent=v.toFixed(2);const cd=.28*13.5/v,focus=(.33/v)**2;opticsWorld.innerHTML='

Smaller is better for printable size

'+cd.toFixed(2)+' nm

Relative focus tolerance (NA 0.33 = 100%)

'+(focus*100).toFixed(1)+'%
NA rises → finer resolution
NA rises → thinner focus window
';}na.oninput=paintOptics;paintOptics();
questions: In the simplified model, increasing NA does what to printable size?
Why is higher NA not a free win?
The focus window scales roughly with inverse NA squared.
What is the status of Hyper-NA here?
Research direction with system-level evidence still needed
The cited work evaluates a potential extension, not a deployed production system.

steps.note: Set illustrative EUV inputs.
Compute the simplified critical-dimension estimate.
Compare focus tolerance with NA 0.33.

walkthrough.limit: Executed local arithmetic only. The equations and chosen k₁ are simplified teaching inputs, not process qualification or vendor performance.

visual_explanation: Two bars move in opposite directions. The first gets shorter as printable size improves; the second collapses faster because focus tolerance scales with NA squared.
written_questions: Which omitted process effect could erase the arithmetic advantage?
What evidence would move Hyper-NA from research claim to roadmap commitment?

title: A merge queue needs tests for the merge group
goal: Configure GitHub Actions so required checks run on the exact candidate the merge queue intends to merge.
concept:
Two musicians can sound fine alone and clash when they play together. A pull request test checks one musician; a merge-group test checks the temporary combination queued for the branch.

When required checks protect a branch that uses GitHub merge queue, the workflow must listen for merge_group. Otherwise the required status may never be reported for the queued candidate, or the combined changes may go untested.
example: PR A changes a schema and PR B changes a client. Each passes against main. The merge queue forms one temporary SHA containing both; its contract test fails. Testing only pull_request misses the interaction.

use_case.when: Use merge_group when a protected branch requires checks and GitHub merge queue is enabled.
use_case.example: A busy monorepo queues multiple approved PRs whose generated clients and schemas can interact.
use_case.decision: Run the same required check name on both pull-request and merge-group events; ensure checkout and caches key off the event SHA, and avoid assuming PR-only fields exist.

practice: Switch the workflow trigger set and see whether the required check reaches the merge-group SHA.
boundary: The browser models event matching only. It does not parse YAML, create a queue, run GitHub Actions, verify permissions or reproduce concurrency and cancellation.
sim:
on:
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]

function paintQueue(){const both=ghaTrigger.value==='both';queueWorld.innerHTML='
PR A SHA
PASS

PASS
merge-group SHA
A+B
required test
'+(both?'RUNS → catches conflict':'NOT REPORTED')+'
';}ghaTrigger.onchange=paintQueue;queueRun.onclick=paintQueue;paintQueue();
questions: Which event makes Actions run for a GitHub merge queue candidate?
The merge_group event targets the temporary queued candidate.
Why can two green PR checks still produce a red merge group?
The candidate contains a composition not tested by either PR alone.
What should checkout test in a merge-group run?
Required status must describe the exact queued candidate.

steps.note: Start with a PR-only workflow and a queued combined SHA.
The queued event does not match the workflow.

steps.code:
events.add('merge_group')

tested_sha=merge_group_sha if required_reported else None
steps.note: Add the event so the exact merge-group SHA is tested.

walkthrough.limit: Executed local Python set membership, not GitHub's event engine or a workflow.

visual_explanation: The first two boxes are individually tested PRs; the third is a new combined SHA. Only the second trigger choice connects the required check to that candidate.
written_questions: Which workflow fields in your CI assume a pull_request payload?
How will cache keys prevent artifacts from one SHA being mistaken for another?

title: One trace ID joins the call path; it does not authenticate it
goal: Read and propagate W3C traceparent while keeping tracing separate from authentication and authorization.
concept:
A baggage tag lets airport staff follow one suitcase across flights. It does not prove the person carrying it owns the suitcase. A trace ID similarly joins spans across services; it is correlation context, not identity or permission.

A traceparent carries version, trace ID, parent span ID and flags. Each receiving service keeps the trace ID, creates its own span ID, and passes that new parent onward. Invalid or unsafe input must be handled deliberately.
example: Gateway, Orders and Payment share trace ID 4bf9…. Orders records Gateway's span as parent, creates span b7ad…, and sends that as Payment's parent. JWT validation and authorization still happen independently.

use_case.when: Use Trace Context across synchronous and asynchronous service boundaries to correlate latency, errors and retries.
use_case.example: Find whether a slow checkout spent time in the gateway, Orders, Payment or a downstream database.
use_case.decision: Propagate valid context through trusted instrumentation, create a new span per operation, and keep auth decisions on verified credentials. Apply sampling, privacy and abuse controls at trust boundaries.

practice: Toggle a valid versus all-zero trace ID and compare propagation with authentication status.
boundary: This browser validates only a tiny subset of the traceparent grammar. It does not create telemetry, enforce trust boundaries, sample traces, verify signatures or authorize requests.
js:
function paintTraceContext(){const valid=traceCase.value==='valid',auth=authOk.checked;traceWorld.innerHTML='
incoming trace
'+(valid?'accept trace-id':'invalid → start/reject per policy')+'
Orders
new span-id
Payment
same trace-id
authorization
'+(auth?'ALLOW':'DENY')+'

Trace result and auth result are independent.

';}[traceCase,authOk].forEach(x=>x.onchange=paintTraceContext);traceRun.onclick=paintTraceContext;paintTraceContext();
questions: What stays the same across spans in one distributed trace?
The shared trace ID correlates the path; each span has its own ID.
Can a valid traceparent authorize a payment?
Trace context is observability metadata, not an authenticated principal.
An all-zero trace ID is received. What does the W3C format say?
All-zero trace and parent IDs are forbidden by the format.

steps.note: Split version, trace ID, parent span ID and flags.

steps.code:
version,trace_id,parent_span_id,flags=parts
valid=(len(trace_id)==32 and int(trace_id,16)!=0 and len(parent_span_id)==16 and int(parent_span_id,16)!=0)
steps.note: Check essential identity constraints for this known version.
Create a child span while keeping authorization separate.

walkthrough.limit: Executed local string parsing with a simplified validator. Production libraries must implement the full specification, limits, forwarding, sampling and security guidance.

visual_explanation: The first three boxes share correlation context, while the authorization box changes independently. This makes the non-authentication boundary visible rather than burying it in prose.
written_questions: At which ingress boundaries will you accept, replace or annotate incoming trace context?
Which credentials—not trace headers—authorize the downstream call?
